test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 20 Nov, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: From where does most of the refracted light rays enter the eyes?

options.text: From the outer surface of the cornea
From the outer surface of the retina
From the outer surface of the iris
From the inner surface of the cornea

solution:
The correct answer is __**From the outer surface of the cornea **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **outer surface of the cornea** is responsible for **most of the refraction of light rays** entering our eyes.
 
• The **cornea** is a **thin membrane** through which the **light rays enter our eyes**.
 
• It forms the **transparent bulge** on the front surface of the eyeball.
 
• **The retina** is one of the three layers of the eye, where **image formation** takes place.
 
• The other two are choroid and sclera.
 
• It is **light-sensitive** in nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iris** is a dark **muscular diaphragm**, present behind the cornea, that **controls the size of the pupil**.
 
• The **eye lens** is **biconvex** in nature and helps in the **adjustment of the focal length** so that the object focuses on the retina.
 
• It forms an **inverted real image** of an object on the retina.
